name: MICRONESIA

flag.title: Four Stars & Ocean
flag.note: Blue for the Pacific; 4 stars for 4 states

lead: The Federated States of Micronesia has 607 islands in the world's biggest ocean. One city sits on a coral reef. Stone wheels were once money. A sunken wartime fleet rests in a lagoon.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Micronesia's 607 islands stretch nearly 3,000 km across the western Pacific. Together they would fit inside London. Most are low coral atolls (rings of reef) with turquoise lagoons.
Pohnpei gets over 7,600 mm of rain a year. It is one of Earth's wettest spots. Between the islands, the ocean plunges 8 km deep.
animals: Over 100 manta rays live in Yap's warm channels. Hawksbill and green turtles nest on quiet beaches. Nearly 1,000 kinds of reef fish dart through the coral.
At dusk, fruit bats fill the sky. Pingelap has huge coconut crabs. They crack coconuts open and live up to 60 years.
culture: On Pohnpei, people share sakau, a drink pounded from a plant root. They pass it in a coconut shell, in order of rank.
Weavers make baskets and clothes from pandanus and hibiscus fibre. Stick dances and standing dances mark every celebration.
history: Ancient Micronesians were master navigators. They read stars, waves and birds to cross thousands of km. Around 1200 AD the Saudeleur dynasty built Nan Madol, 100 stone islands joined by canals.
Spain, Germany, then Japan ruled in turn. In 1944 a US air attack sank over 60 Japanese ships at Chuuk. The FSM became self-governing in 1979 and fully independent in 1986.
wows: Nan Madol is the only ancient city built on a coral reef, using basalt logs.
Yap's rai stones can weigh 4 tonnes, yet owners change without moving them.
Chuuk Lagoon holds over 60 WWII ships and 200 aircraft.
On Pingelap, 1 in 10 people has total colour blindness, from a 1775 typhoon survivor.
The FSM's ocean is 5 times the size of France, but its land is smaller than Houston.
Operation Christmas Drop has airlifted gifts to remote islands each December since 1952.
Nanlaud peak is so cloud-wrapped that it was not fully surveyed until the 20th century.

myths.fact: They are different parts of the Pacific. Polynesia includes Hawaiʻi, Samoa and Tonga, thousands of km away.
No bat is blind. Fruit bats see well in dim light.
